items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: Well, first thing you know, I was playing in Fisher's Band... His right name was Phillips... He had a brass band... I led the band with one trumpet by myself.

ctx.x: Well, my father, he was the leader of our little junior band we had. His name was? And his name was Henry Brunus. Henry, too. Yeah. And he had my sister playing guitar. One of my other brothers playing guitar. He had to wait for him out. My brother Rudy playing guitar. And little Henny had to stand on a chair to play string bass. And I was the only one that didn't play anything. So my dad used to take us around to places on Saturday nights when he got through. He's White Baker. He was a baker. And he brought us…
His right name was Phillips, but they used to give him that name Fisher. Fisher. He's dead now. Well, it wasn't his real name. No, Phillips.

What sort of a band did he have? He had a brass band. And we used to play at the Crescent Park and Gretna. And they all used to use two and three trumpets for ten men or twelve men brass. I led the band with one trumpet by myself. They called me what they called the Iron Lick Conniprass. And we used to get on the levee in front of the park, and they used to hear me blow way back on St. Charles Avenue when we were playing music.
